title: Rent Policy Impact Simulator — Berlin
methodology: A/B testing framework: counterfactual what-if analysis on Berlin Mietspiegel data. Uses two-sample z-tests with MDE calculations at α=0.05, power=0.80.

mde.description: Minimum detectable effect for Berlin (σ=€3.27/m², n=361 grid cells)
mde.interpretation: Can detect a €0.28/m² rent change (2.3% of Berlin avg €12.07) with 80% power at α=0.05

scenarios.hypothesis: H₀: No change vs H₁: μ_after > μ_before
scenarios.verdict: Massive impact — €482M/yr across 1M+ units. A 5% Mietspiegel hike would shift ~€0.5B annually from tenants to landlords.

scenarios.hypothesis: H₀: No change vs H₁: μ_after > μ_before
scenarios.verdict: Doubles the +5% impact linearly. At this level, 30%+ of median-income households cross the affordability threshold.

counterfactuals.scenario: C: Berlin at Munich rent levels
counterfactuals.hypothesis: H₀: μ_berlin = μ_munich vs H₁: μ_berlin < μ_munich
counterfactuals.verdict: Berlin rents would jump 65% to match Munich. ~€632M annual impact. Statistically significant at p < 0.001.

counterfactuals.scenario: D: Berlin at Leipzig rent levels
counterfactuals.hypothesis: H₀: μ_berlin = μ_leipzig vs H₁: μ_berlin > μ_leipzig
counterfactuals.verdict: Berlin rents would drop 37% to match Leipzig. ~€356M annual savings for tenants. Demonstrates East-West rent divide.
